Chloe / team — quick technical update from infra:

What we see so far:
- Node pool: shared-hosting pool alpha-7, observed queue depth growth on GPU-3 (serving shard) starting 08:08:54.
- TCP retransmits and socket resets between proxy and runtime around 08:09:10.
- Several long GC pauses on runtime process (pause durations 80-140ms) correlated with large request batches.
- Chunked transfer watcher on the proxy side timed out after 60s and returned a 504 to the client in a subset of sessions. The runtime did resume and produced tokens after the quiet window.

Immediate mitigations proposed (can be executed in parallel):
1) Scale up pool alpha-7 by +2 GPUs (hot add) to drain the queue. Risk: brief routing flaps for active connections.
2) Enable the lower-throughput model fallback for Lyra to reduce per-request execution time (config change, instant toggle).
3) Increase chunked transfer timeout and move affected sessions to the keepalive-preserve path.

Impact/ask for exec: if we move Lyra to a reserved/Dedicated pool temporarily it will reduce multi-tenant interference. That requires approval for emergency capacity allocation. Ben — please confirm commercial implications.

I'll keep the incident notes in SUP-4219 and post logs to the Jira link.

Marissa
